Apple___Apple_scab.description: Apple scab is one of the most serious fungal diseases affecting apples and crabapples, causing olive-green to black lesions on leaves and dark scabby spots on fruit.
Apple___Apple_scab.symptoms: Dull olive-green velvety spots on leaves that turn dark brown or black with age; premature leaf drop; fruit developing corky, scabby lesions that may crack.
Apple___Apple_scab.management: Rake and destroy fallen leaves in autumn; prune trees to improve air circulation and sunlight penetration; apply preventative copper or sulfur-based fungicides during bud break and wet spring periods.

Apple___Black_rot.description: Black rot attacks apple fruit, leaves, and bark, leading to 'frog-eye' leaf spots and mummified black fruit.
Apple___Black_rot.symptoms: Circular brown leaf spots with distinct purple margins ('frog-eye'); sunken cankers on limbs; fruit rot turning completely black and mummifying on the branch.
Apple___Black_rot.management: Prune out dead wood and fire-blighted twigs; remove mummified fruits from trees and ground; apply captan or thiophanate-methyl fungicides during early season.

Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.description: A heteroecious rust requiring both apple trees and eastern red cedar / juniper to complete its complex two-year life cycle.
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.symptoms: Bright yellow-orange or reddish circular spots on upper leaf surfaces; raised tube-like structures (aecia) protruding from the underside of leaves.
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.management: Eradicate nearby cedar or juniper hosts if feasible within a 1-2 mile radius; plant rust-resistant apple cultivars; apply myclobutanil or mancozeb fungicides as leaves emerge.

Apple___healthy.description: Vibrant, green apple foliage free of fungal, bacterial, or necrotic lesions.
Apple___healthy.symptoms: Uniform green coloration, smooth margins, well-developed venation, no spotting or curling.
Apple___healthy.management: Continue balanced fertilization, regular irrigation schedule, seasonal pruning, and proactive scouting for early pest or disease pressure.

Blueberry___healthy.description: Healthy blueberry foliage showing lush, uniform green coloration.
Blueberry___healthy.symptoms: No chlorosis, leaf spots, or necrotic margins; firm and glossy foliage.
Blueberry___healthy.management: Maintain acidic soil pH (4.5 to 5.2), provide organic pine bark mulch, ensure steady moisture without waterlogging, and test micronutrients annually.

Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.description: A widespread fungal disease that covers tender cherry leaves and fruit in white powdery fungal mycelia and spores.
Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.symptoms: White powdery patches on leaf surfaces; leaf curling upward; stunted young shoot growth; deformed or cracked fruit.
Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.management: Prune interior canopy to maximize airflow; avoid overhead irrigation; apply potassium bicarbonate, neem oil, or sulfur fungicides at first appearance of powdery growth.

Cherry_(including_sour)___healthy.description: Healthy cherry foliage with robust chlorophyll density and unblemished margins.
Cherry_(including_sour)___healthy.symptoms: Intact leaf blades, vibrant green color, free from fungal spotting or shot-hole perforations.
Cherry_(including_sour)___healthy.management: Standard orchard maintenance: monitor for aphid activity, prune during dormant season, and ensure proper drainage.

Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.description: A devastating fungal disease of corn characterized by rectangular lesions that follow the leaf veins, leading to extensive photosynthetic loss.
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.symptoms: Narrow, rectangular lesions restricted by leaf veins; lesions expand from tan to gray; severe infections result in leaf blight and stalk rot.
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.management: Rotate crops with non-host species (such as soybeans); utilize minimum 2-year tillage to bury crop residue; plant resistant corn hybrids; apply strobilurin or triazole fungicides.

Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.description: Fungal rust causing powdery pustules across both upper and lower corn leaf surfaces, favored by cool, humid weather.
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.symptoms: Small, oval, cinnamon-brown to dark brown powdery pustules (uredinia) scattered on leaves; rupture of the leaf epidermis.
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.management: Plant resistant hybrids with specific Rp gene resistance; early planting to avoid peak spore dispersal; apply foliar fungicides when pustules appear on upper leaves before silking.

Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.description: A major foliar disease causing large, cigar-shaped grayish-green to tan lesions on corn leaves, causing significant grain yield reduction.
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.symptoms: Long, elliptical (cigar-shaped) lesions (1 to 6 inches long) starting on lower leaves and progressing upwards; lesions turn tan or grayish with dark fungal spores.
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.management: Use resistant hybrids containing Ht genes; practice crop rotation; incorporate crop residue into soil; apply registered fungicides if disease reaches the ear leaf prior to tasseling.

Corn_(maize)___healthy.description: Vigorous, dark green maize foliage without necrotic stripes, pustules, or chlorotic streaks.
Corn_(maize)___healthy.symptoms: Clean, elongated leaf blades with distinct central midrib and uniform green coloration.
Corn_(maize)___healthy.management: Apply nitrogen according to soil tests, maintain adequate moisture during silking, and scout fields regularly.

Grape___Black_rot.description: A destructive disease affecting cultivated grapevines, attacking shoots, leaves, and causing infected fruit to shrivel into hard black mummies.
Grape___Black_rot.symptoms: Small circular reddish-brown leaf spots with tiny black dots (pycnidia) inside the ring; berries turn soft, rot, and shrivel into black mummies.
Grape___Black_rot.management: Prune and destroy infected canes and mummified clusters; open the vine canopy through shoot thinning; apply myclobutanil or mancozeb from early shoot growth through fruit set.

Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).pathogen: Complex of Phaeomoniella chlamydospora & Fomitiporia mediterranea
Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).description: A complex trunk and foliar disease that causes characteristic 'tiger-stripe' necrosis on leaves and dark flecks on grapes.
Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).symptoms: 'Tiger-stripe' chlorotic and necrotic patterns between leaf veins; sudden wilting ('apoplexy') of whole shoots in hot weather; purple-brown spots on fruit.
Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).management: Protect pruning wounds with wound sealants; avoid pruning in rainy weather; remove and burn dead trunks; replace severely infected vines.

Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.description: Causes irregular brown to dark reddish necrotic lesions that lead to premature defoliation in late summer.
Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.symptoms: Irregular necrotic brown lesions with faint yellowish halos; dark fungal sporulation visible on the underside in humid conditions.
Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.management: Improve air circulation in the vineyard canopy; remove fallen leaf debris; apply copper fungicides or broad-spectrum protectants.

Grape___healthy.description: Healthy grapevine leaf showing classic lobed morphology and uniform green pigment.
Grape___healthy.symptoms: Well-expanded palmate leaf blades, clear venation, absence of spots, wilting, or marginal burns.
Grape___healthy.management: Maintain trellis training, balanced fertigation, cover cropping, and integrated pest management against powdery and downy mildew.

Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).description: Citrus greening (HLB) is one of the world's most devastating citrus diseases, vectored by the Asian citrus psyllid (Diaphorina citri).
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).symptoms: Asymmetric blotchy mottling on leaves crossing leaf veins; yellow shoots; small, misshapen, bitter fruit that remains green at the base; tree dieback.
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).management: Control Asian citrus psyllid populations using targeted insecticides or biological controls; plant certified disease-free nursery stock; remove and destroy infected trees to prevent orchard spread.

Peach___Bacterial_spot.description: Bacterial disease causing angular shot-hole spots on leaves and sunken crater-like lesions on peach fruit.
Peach___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small water-soaked polygonal spots that turn purple-black; dead centers drop out creating a 'shot-hole' appearance; fruit cracking and gumming.
Peach___Bacterial_spot.management: Plant tolerant peach varieties; avoid excessive nitrogen fertilizer; apply copper sprays during dormant and bud-swell stages; apply oxytetracycline during early fruit development.

Peach___healthy.description: Healthy lanceolate peach foliage with smooth margins and glossy green surface.
Peach___healthy.symptoms: Vibrant green blades without shot holes, leaf curl, or marginal scorch.
Peach___healthy.management: Dormant preventative copper sprays for peach leaf curl, weed management around root zones, and balanced irrigation.

Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.description: Common bacterial disease of peppers in warm, humid regions, causing significant defoliation and unmarketable fruit.
Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small circular water-soaked leaf spots that become dark brown with yellow halos; severe defoliation exposing peppers to sunscald; blister-like scab on fruit.
Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.management: Use certified pathogen-free seed; sanitize transplant trays and equipment; avoid overhead watering; spray preventative copper bactericides mixed with mancozeb.

Pepper,_bell___healthy.description: Healthy bell pepper leaf showing vibrant green tissue without spots or mosaic patterns.
Pepper,_bell___healthy.symptoms: Smooth ovate leaves, firm structure, uniform coloration.
Pepper,_bell___healthy.management: Ensure adequate calcium to prevent blossom end rot, stake plants for support, and monitor for aphids and thrips.

Potato___Early_blight.description: Foliar fungal disease characterized by concentric target-ring spots on older potato leaves, leading to reduced tuber yields.
Potato___Early_blight.symptoms: Dark brown circular spots with distinct concentric rings ('target-board' pattern); surrounding yellow halos; lower leaves turn yellow and drop.
Potato___Early_blight.management: Practice 3-year crop rotation with non-solanaceous crops; maintain good vine vigor with balanced nitrogen; apply chlorothalonil or azoxystrobin fungicides preventatively.

Potato___Late_blight.description: The catastrophic disease responsible for the Irish Potato Famine; spreads rapidly during cool, wet weather, destroying entire fields in days.
Potato___Late_blight.symptoms: Large, irregular water-soaked pale green or dark brown lesions; white cottony fungal growth on the underside of leaves in humid conditions; tubers rot with a foul odor.
Potato___Late_blight.management: Destroy cull piles; plant certified disease-free seed tubers; eliminate volunteer potato plants; apply systemic fungicides like mandipropamid or cymoxanil upon local disease warnings.

Potato___healthy.description: Lush compound potato foliage showing healthy leaf venation and no necrosis.
Potato___healthy.symptoms: Firm leaflets, deep green color, free from spots, blight, or viral mosaics.
Potato___healthy.management: Hill soil over developing tubers, maintain consistent soil moisture, and follow IPM scouting protocols.

Raspberry___healthy.description: Healthy compound raspberry leaf with serrated margins and vibrant green appearance.
Raspberry___healthy.symptoms: Clean serrated margins, white-felted underside typical of healthy canes, no rust or anthracnose.
Raspberry___healthy.management: Prune out spent floricanes after harvest; thin primocanes to enhance ventilation; maintain organic mulch.

Soybean___healthy.description: Healthy trifoliate soybean leaf with intact structure and active photosynthetic area.
Soybean___healthy.symptoms: Uniform green trifoliate leaflets, absence of frogeye leaf spots, rust, or sudden death syndrome chlorosis.
Soybean___healthy.management: Standard agronomic practices: inoculate with Bradyrhizobium japonicum, scout for soybean aphids, and implement crop rotation.

Squash___Powdery_mildew.description: Ubiquitous fungal infection coating squash leaves in powdery white spores, causing leaves to brown and wither prematurely.
Squash___Powdery_mildew.symptoms: White talcum-powder-like spots on both leaf surfaces; spots coalesce to cover entire leaves; affected leaves turn yellow, brown, and brittle.
Squash___Powdery_mildew.management: Plant powdery-mildew-resistant squash varieties; provide wide plant spacing for sunlight penetration; apply potassium bicarbonate, horticultural oils, or sulfur fungicides.

Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.description: Common foliar disease of strawberries causing numerous small purple-to-brown spots that merge until leaves appear burned or scorched.
Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.symptoms: Irregular dark purple to reddish-brown blotches (1 to 5 mm) lacking pale centers; leaves curl upward and dry out as if scorched by heat.
Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.management: Plant certified disease-free runners; renovate strawberry beds after harvest by mowing old foliage; avoid overhead sprinklers; apply captan or fenhexamid.

Strawberry___healthy.description: Healthy trifoliate strawberry foliage exhibiting deep emerald green color.
Strawberry___healthy.symptoms: Firm serrated leaflets, free of leaf spot, scorch, or spider mite webbing.
Strawberry___healthy.management: Mulch with clean straw to prevent fruit-soil contact, provide drip irrigation, and remove old dead leaves.

Tomato___Bacterial_spot.description: Bacterial infection causing small, water-soaked, dark spots on tomato foliage, stems, and fruit.
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small (1-3 mm) angular dark brown spots with greasy texture; yellowing of surrounding leaf tissue; defoliation; blister-like scabs on green tomatoes.
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.management: Use certified disease-free seed; avoid touching wet foliage; sanitize stakes and cages; spray copper hydroxide combined with mancozeb or bacteriophages.

Tomato___Early_blight.description: Fungal disease causing concentric target-ring spots on older foliage, progressively killing leaves from bottom to top.
Tomato___Early_blight.symptoms: Dark brown spots with concentric rings ('bullseye' appearance) surrounded by chlorotic yellow halo; lower leaves wither and drop; collar rot on seedling stems.
Tomato___Early_blight.management: Stake and prune lower leaves 12 inches above the soil line; apply mulch around the base to prevent soil splash; apply copper or chlorothalonil fungicides.

Tomato___Late_blight.description: Extremely fast-moving water-mold disease that devastates tomato plants during cool, rainy weather.
Tomato___Late_blight.symptoms: Large, dark greasy-looking lesions on leaves and stems; white fuzzy sporulation on leaf undersides in high humidity; firm, greasy brown rot on tomatoes.
Tomato___Late_blight.management: Immediately pull and bag heavily infected plants to stop spore drift; avoid overhead watering; apply preventative bio-fungicides or chlorothalonil upon weather alert.

Tomato___Leaf_Mold.description: A fungal disease predominantly affecting greenhouse and high-tunnel tomatoes in conditions of high humidity (>85%).
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.symptoms: Pale greenish-yellow spots with indistinct margins on upper leaf surfaces; olive-green to brown velvety fungal growth directly below on leaf undersides.
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.management: Improve ventilation and air circulation with fans; maintain relative humidity below 80%; prune lower leaves; plant resistant varieties (e.g., with Cf genes).

Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.description: One of the most destructive foliar diseases of tomatoes, producing hundreds of tiny circular spots that defoliate plants.
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.symptoms: Small, circular spots (1-3 mm) with dark brown margins and sunken grayish-white centers dotted with tiny black fruiting bodies (pycnidia).
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.management: Avoid overhead watering; remove and dispose of infected bottom leaves promptly; practice 3-year crop rotation; apply copper or chlorothalonil fungicides.

Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.description: Microscopic sap-feeding arachnids that puncture plant cells, favored by hot, dry conditions, creating fine webbing on undersides of leaves.
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.symptoms: Fine yellow or white stippling on leaf surfaces; bronzed, dry foliage; delicate silky webbing on leaf undersides and growing tips.
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.management: Spray undersides of leaves with strong streams of water; release predatory mites (Phytoseiulus persimilis); apply insecticidal soap or neem oil; avoid excessive synthetic pyrethroids.

Tomato___Target_Spot.description: Fungal pathogen causing circular lesions with light brown centers and dark concentric rings on leaves and sunken lesions on fruit.
Tomato___Target_Spot.symptoms: Brown circular spots with concentric target-pattern rings; lesions can coalesce to cause blighting and leaf collapse.
Tomato___Target_Spot.management: Ensure adequate plant spacing; remove lower diseased foliage; avoid overhead watering; apply strobilurin or carboxamide fungicides.

Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.description: A destructive viral disease transmitted by the silverleaf whitefly, causing severe plant stunting and drastic fruit abortion.
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.symptoms: Upward curling and cupping of leaflets; strong interveinal chlorosis (yellowing) on leaf margins; pronounced plant stunting and bushy growth; flowers drop off.
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.management: Control whitefly vectors using yellow sticky cards and systemic insecticides; use UV-reflective silver mulches; install insect-exclusion netting; plant TYLCV-resistant hybrids.

Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.description: Highly stable and contagious virus transmitted via tools, worker hands, seeds, and root contact, causing mottling and distorted growth.
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.symptoms: Alternating light and dark green mosaic patterns on leaves; blistered, distorted or strap-like foliage; internal browning (brown wall) of tomato fruit.
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.management: Wash hands with soap and disinfect pruning tools with 20% skim milk or 10% bleach; plant certified virus-free seed; burn or bury infected plants; avoid smoking near tomatoes.

Tomato___healthy.description: Vibrant, deep green tomato foliage with robust hairs (trichomes) and intact serrated leaflet margins.
Tomato___healthy.symptoms: Uniform rich green coloration, absence of spotting, mottling, or wilt.
Tomato___healthy.management: Stake or cage plants, mulch root zone, provide consistent drip irrigation, and maintain weekly scouting for foliar blights.
